title: Short Stuff: The Coconut Cult
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Coconut Cult. Josh and Chuck discuss the Sanskrit name for the coconut tree (kalpa vriksha, 'tree which gives all that is necessary for living') and how it is wrong. They profile August Engelhardt, a German born in 1875 who was influenced by the Lebensreform life reform movement, believed the sun was the source of life and coconuts were closest to the sun like the brain, and moved in the early 1900s to the small island of Kabakan off Papua New Guinea to live naked on a coconut-only diet. Coconuts lack key vitamins and protein, and he wasted away. He attracted followers through his book 'A Carefree Future: The New Gospel' and correspondence. Heinrich Jukins, a vegetarian, and Max Lutzow, a concert pianist, arrived; Jukins died within weeks, and Lutzow died after a dispute over music led him to spend a night on a missionary boat and a storm kept him from returning. Hosts compare the New York Times 1905 account (only two followers came) with a How Stuff Works article that says more people arrived and died later, including from dehydration, heat stroke, and a coconut falling on someone. Engelhardt was nursed by a missionary boat crew, returned to the island, was held as a prisoner of war during World War I, and died in 1919 at 44 weighing under 70 pounds.

segments.title: Opening banter and Sanskrit coconut name
segments.summary: Hosts joke about the show setup, then introduce the Sanskrit name for the coconut tree, kalpa vriksha, meaning tree which gives all that is necessary for living, and note that it is not literally true.

segments.title: August Engelhardt's life reform beliefs
segments.summary: Engelhardt, born 1875 in Germany, was drawn to the Lebensreform movement and believed the sun was the source of life and coconuts were closest to the sun like the brain. The hosts compare his views to Goop.

segments.title: Move to Kabakan island
segments.summary: Engelhardt inherited money, bought 185 acres on Kabakan island off New Guinea, and lived naked on a coconut diet, believing humans evolved in the subtropics. He wasted away because coconuts lack key vitamins and protein.

segments.title: Followers arrive and the New York Times account
segments.summary: Engelhardt attracted followers through his book and letters. The hosts contrast the New York Times 1905 article, which says only two men came, with the How Stuff Works account. Heinrich Jukins died within weeks and Max Lutzow, a concert pianist, fought with Engelhardt over music.

segments.title: Deaths on the island and Engelhardt's later years
segments.summary: Lutzow spent a night on a missionary boat and died after a storm kept him from returning. Later visitors died, including one from a falling coconut. Engelhardt was rescued by missionaries, returned to the island, was held as a prisoner in World War I, and died in 1919 at 44, weighing under 70 pounds.

segments.title: Closing and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts joke about Engelhardt being married to a coconut and sign off, noting the show is a production of iHeartRadio's How Stuff Works.
